questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used to distinguish primary and secondary amines by Hinsberg test.
questions.solution:
Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines.

The reagent used in this test is benzenesulfonyl chloride, which has the chemical formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$.

Primary amines react with Hinsberg reagent to form an N-alkylbenzenesulfonamide, which is soluble in alkali due to the presence of an acidic hydrogen attached to nitrogen.

Secondary amines react to form an N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamide, which is insoluble in alkali as it lacks an acidic hydrogen.

Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg reagent.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline on treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2$ / HCl at about $0^\circ\text{C}$ gives a compound A, which on further treatment with CuCN / KCN gives a compound B, which when reacts with $\text{H}_2$ / Ni gives a compound C. The compound C on reaction with $\text{HNO}_2$ gives a compound D. The structure of D is:
questions.solution:
Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) undergoes diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and HCl at $0^\circ\text{C}$ to form benzene diazonium chloride (A).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}, 0^\circ\text{C}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ (A)

Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with CuCN / KCN to form benzonitrile (B) via the Sandmeyer reaction.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN} / \text{KCN}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$ (B)

Benzonitrile is reduced by $\text{H}_2$ / Ni to form benzylamine (C).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (C)

Benzylamine, being an aliphatic primary amine, reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) to form benzyl alcohol (D) with the evolution of nitrogen gas.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (D)

Therefore, the structure of D is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{-OH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{-OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the substrate 'A' in the following reaction.
$\text{A} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{ii)}\ \Delta}]{\large{\text{i) Moist Ag}_2\text{O}}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{N(CH}_3)_2 + \text{CH}_2 = \text{CH}_2$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the Hofmann elimination of a quaternary ammonium salt.

Substrate A reacts with moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ to form a quaternary ammonium hydroxide, which on heating undergoes $\beta$-elimination to yield an alkene, a tertiary amine, and water.

The products obtained are $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{N(CH}_3)_2$ (N,N-dimethylethylamine) and $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ (ethene).

The quaternary ammonium ion must contain the alkyl groups present in the tertiary amine along with the alkyl group that underwent elimination to form the alkene. Combining an ethyl group (from ethene) with N,N-dimethylethylamine gives the diethyldimethylammonium ion, $[(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2)_2\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2]^+$.

Since moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ is used in the first step to replace a halide ion with a hydroxide ion, substrate A must be a halide.

Therefore, substrate A is diethyldimethylammonium halide.

Answer: Diethyldimethylammonium halide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following reactions occurs by removal of -CO- group from amide ?
questions.solution:
Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction involves the conversion of a primary amide to a primary amine with one carbon atom less than the original amide.

The general reaction is given by:

$R-CO-NH_2 + Br_2 + 4NaOH \rightarrow R-NH_2 + Na_2CO_3 + 2NaBr + 2H_2O$

In this reaction, the carbonyl group ($-CO-$) is removed from the amide as sodium carbonate.

Answer: Hofmann degradation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines is obtained by Gabrial phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used exclusively for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.

Phthalimide on treatment with ethanolic potassium hydroxide forms the potassium salt of phthalimide, which on heating with an alkyl halide followed by alkaline hydrolysis produces the corresponding primary amine.

Aromatic primary amines like $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

Secondary and tertiary amines like $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ cannot be prepared by this method.

Among the given options, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ is the only primary aliphatic amine and can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is obtained when propionamide is treated with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH solution ?
questions.solution:
Propionamide is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction of an amide with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH is known as the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

In this reaction, the amide is converted into a primary amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{KBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The product obtained is ethylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines when heated with ethanolic KOH and chloroform does NOT produce foul smell ?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and ethanolic KOH to produce a foul-smelling compound is known as the carbylamine test or isocyanide test.

This test is given only by primary aliphatic and primary aromatic amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Benzenamine is a primary aromatic amine.

Propan-2-amine is a primary aliphatic amine.

Phenylmethanamine is a primary aliphatic amine.

N,N-Dimethyl aniline is a tertiary amine, so it does not give the carbylamine test and will not produce a foul smell.

Answer: N , N - Dimethyl aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify 'B' in the following reaction
Ethyl cyanide $\xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_2\text{O}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_2\text{O / dil HCl}}} \text{B} + \text{NH}_3$
questions.solution:
Ethyl cyanide is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.

Partial hydrolysis of ethyl cyanide yields propanamide (A).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$

Complete hydrolysis of propanamide in the presence of dilute $\text{HCl}$ yields propanoic acid (B) and ammonia.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O} / \text{dil HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_3$

Therefore, B is propanoic acid.

Answer: Propanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of hydrogen atoms needed to obtain one mole ethanamine from acetamide using $\text{LiAl H}_4$ /ether as reducing agent.
questions.solution:
The chemical reaction for the reduction of acetamide to ethanamine using $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is:

$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4/\text{ether}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

In this process, the carbonyl oxygen is removed as a water molecule, which consumes two hydrogen atoms. The carbonyl carbon is reduced to a methylene group ($\text{CH}_2$), which consumes another two hydrogen atoms.

Thus, a total of $4$ moles of hydrogen atoms are required to reduce one mole of acetamide to one mole of ethanamine.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT correct regarding Hofmann's exhaustive alkylation?
options: In this quaternary ammmonium salts are obtained.
Two moles of alkylhalide when heated with one mole primary amine forms tetraalkyl ammonium halide.
Depending on the quantity of alkyl halides treated with primary amine, the mixture of secondary and tertiary amines obtained.
The reaction is carried out in presence of $\text{NaHCO}_3$
questions.solution:
Hofmann's exhaustive alkylation is the process of converting an amine into a quaternary ammonium salt by treating it with an excess of alkyl halide.

When a primary amine ($RNH_2$) is heated with an alkyl halide ($RX$), it undergoes successive nucleophilic substitution reactions:
$RNH_2 + RX \rightarrow R_2NH + HX$ (Secondary amine)
$R_2NH + RX \rightarrow R_3N + HX$ (Tertiary amine)
$R_3N + RX \rightarrow R_4N^+X^-$ (Quaternary ammonium salt)

To convert one mole of a primary amine into a tetraalkyl ammonium halide, three moles of alkyl halide are required, not two. Therefore, the statement that two moles of alkyl halide form a tetraalkyl ammonium halide is incorrect.

The reaction is typically carried out in the presence of a mild base like $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to neutralize the acid ($HX$) formed, which prevents the protonation of the amine and maintains its nucleophilicity. Depending on the stoichiometric ratio of the reactants, a mixture of secondary and tertiary amines can also be obtained.

Answer: Two moles of alkylhalide when heated with one mole primary amine forms tetraalkyl ammonium halide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines does NOT form alkyl isocyanide when heated with alc. KOH and chloroform
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to form an alkyl isocyanide is known as the carbylamine reaction.

This test is given only by primary (aliphatic and aromatic) amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Methanamine, propan-2-amine, and ethanamine are primary amines, so they will form alkyl isocyanides.

N, N-Diethylethanamine is a tertiary amine, hence it does not undergo the carbylamine reaction and will not form an alkyl isocyanide.

Answer: N, N-Diethylethanamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify false statement from following regarding preparation of amines by Hofmann degradation method.
options: It is useful to convert amides to primary amines.
In this -CO-group is reduced to $-\text{CH}_2-$ group.
Molar mass of the amine obtained is always less than the amide.
questions.solution:
Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction is used for the conversion of primary amides to primary amines with one carbon atom less than the original amide.

The general reaction is:
$R-CO-NH_2 + Br_2 + 4KOH \rightarrow R-NH_2 + K_2CO_3 + 2KBr + 2H_2O$

In this reaction, the carbonyl group ($-CO-$) is lost as potassium carbonate ($K_2CO_3$), and the alkyl or aryl group migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom. The $-CO-$ group is not reduced to a $-CH_2-$ group. The reduction of an amide to an amine where the $-CO-$ group becomes a $-CH_2-$ group is achieved using strong reducing agents like $LiAlH_4$.

Since the product amine has one carbon less than the reactant amide, its molar mass is always less than that of the amide.

Thus, the statement that the $-CO-$ group is reduced to a $-CH_2-$ group is false.

Answer: In this -CO-group is reduced to $-\text{CH}_2-$ group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines when heated with ethanolic KOH and chloroform forms aryl isocyanide ?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and ethanolic KOH to form an isocyanide is known as the carbylamine reaction.

This reaction is a characteristic test given only by primary aliphatic and primary aromatic amines.

Among the given options, benzenamine (aniline) is a primary aromatic amine, while N-methylaniline and ethylethanamine are secondary amines, and N,N-dimethylaniline is a tertiary amine.

Therefore, benzenamine reacts with chloroform and ethanolic KOH to form phenyl isocyanide (an aryl isocyanide).

$C_6H_5NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow C_6H_5NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$

Answer: Benzenamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify correct decreasing order of basic strength of amines
questions.solution:
Basic strength of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In aliphatic amines, the electron-donating $+I$ effect of alkyl groups increases the electron density on nitrogen, making them more basic than ammonia. For methylamines in aqueous solution, the combined effect of the $+I$ effect, steric hindrance, and hydration energy results in the basic strength order: secondary > primary > tertiary. Thus, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3$.

In aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$), the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalized over the benzene ring due to resonance. This decreases the availability of the lone pair for protonation, making aniline less basic than ammonia.

Combining these factors, the correct decreasing order of basic strength is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3 \gt \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3 \gt \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the major product obtained when ethyl amine is reacted with excess of methyl iodide ?
questions.solution:
Ethyl amine reacts with excess of methyl iodide to undergo exhaustive methylation, forming a quaternary ammonium salt.

$C_2H_5NH_2 + CH_3I \rightarrow C_2H_5NHCH_3 + HI$

$C_2H_5NHCH_3 + CH_3I \rightarrow C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2 + HI$

$C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2 + CH_3I \rightarrow [C_2H_5N(CH_3)_3]^+ I^-$

Since methyl iodide is in excess, the reaction does not stop at the secondary or tertiary amine stage but proceeds to the final quaternary ammonium salt.

The major product obtained is ethyltrimethylammonium iodide.

Answer: Ethyltrimethylammonium iodide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Tertiary amines have the lowest boiling points because ,
options: They possess inter-molecular dipole-dipole attraction forces.
They do not possess inter-molecular H- bonding
questions.solution:
Tertiary amines have the general formula $R_3N$. Since there are no hydrogen atoms directly attached to the highly electronegative nitrogen atom, they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

In contrast, primary and secondary amines have hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen and can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which leads to higher boiling points.

Due to the absence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding, tertiary amines have the lowest boiling points among isomeric amines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Primary amines show intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
Tertiary butylamine is a primary amine.
Tertiary amines do not show inter molecular hydrogen bonds.
questions.solution:
Primary amines have the general formula $R-NH_2$. Since they have two hydrogen atoms attached to the highly electronegative nitrogen atom, they can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Tertiary butylamine has the structure $(CH_3)_3C-NH_2$. The nitrogen atom is attached to only one carbon atom, making it a primary amine.

Tertiary amines have the general formula $R_3N$. They do not have any hydrogen atoms attached to the nitrogen atom, so they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other.

iso-propylamine has the structure $(CH_3)_2CH-NH_2$. The nitrogen atom is attached to only one carbon atom. Therefore, it is a primary amine, not a secondary amine. The classification of amines depends on the number of alkyl groups attached to the nitrogen atom, not the degree of the carbon atom it is attached to.

Answer: iso-propylamine is a secondary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions uses diazonium salt ?
questions.solution:
The Sandmeyer reaction involves the conversion of an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide using copper(I) salts, such as $CuCl$ or $CuBr$.

The Mendius reaction is the reduction of nitriles to primary amines using sodium and ethanol.

The Hofmann rearrangement reaction involves the conversion of a primary amide to a primary amine with one fewer carbon atom using bromine and a strong base.

The carbylamine reaction is a test for primary amines, where a primary amine reacts with chloroform and a base to form an isocyanide.

Therefore, only the Sandmeyer reaction uses a diazonium salt.

Answer: Sandmeyer reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amines is not represented by formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ ?
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ corresponds to saturated acyclic amines.

The possible structural isomers are:

Primary ($1^\circ$) amines: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (propan-1-amine) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (propan-2-amine).

Secondary ($2^\circ$) amine: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ (N-methylethanamine).

Tertiary ($3^\circ$) amine: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ (N,N-dimethylmethanamine).

A quaternary ammonium salt requires the nitrogen atom to be bonded to four alkyl groups. The simplest quaternary ammonium salt is the tetramethylammonium ion, which contains four carbon atoms ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{12}\text{N}^+$).

Thus, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ cannot represent a quaternary ammonium salt.

Answer: quaternary ammonium salt

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify Hinsberg's reagent from following.
questions.solution:
Hinsberg's reagent is benzene sulphonyl chloride ($C_6H_5SO_2Cl$).

It is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines.

Primary amines react with it to form a precipitate that is soluble in alkali.

Secondary amines react to form a precipitate that is insoluble in alkali.

Tertiary amines do not react with it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{I} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{B}$
questions.solution:
Methyl iodide reacts with potassium cyanide to undergo nucleophilic substitution, forming methyl cyanide (acetonitrile) as product A.

$\text{CH}_3\text{I} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CN} \text{ (A)} + \text{KI}$

Methyl cyanide undergoes Mendius reduction in the presence of sodium and ethanol to form ethylamine as product B.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \text{ (B)}$

Thus, product B is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2$.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of amine is Iso propyl amine ?
questions.solution:
The structure of isopropyl amine is $(CH_3)_2CH-NH_2$.

In amines, the degree of the amine is determined by the number of alkyl or aryl groups directly attached to the nitrogen atom.

Since the nitrogen atom in isopropyl amine is attached to only one carbon atom (the isopropyl group), it is classified as a primary amine.

Answer: primary amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amines is not obtained by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.

In this reaction, potassium phthalimide is treated with an alkyl halide to form an N-alkyl phthalimide, which upon hydrolysis yields a primary amine.

Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion because the carbon-halogen bond in aryl halides has partial double bond character due to resonance, making it difficult to break.

Hence, primary aromatic amines such as aniline cannot be prepared by this method.

Benzyl amine, methyl amine, and isobutyl amine are primary aliphatic amines and can be successfully prepared by this method.

Answer: Aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following reagents is used to prepare alkyl isocyanides from RX?
questions.solution:
Alkyl halides react with alcoholic silver cyanide ($\text{AgCN}$) to form alkyl isocyanides as the major product.

$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly covalent in nature, so only the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons available for nucleophilic attack. This leads to the formation of an alkyl isocyanide ($\text{RNC}$).

$\text{R-X} + \text{AgCN} \rightarrow \text{R-NC} + \text{AgX}$

In contrast, $\text{KCN}$ gives alkyl cyanides, $\text{KNO}_2$ gives alkyl nitrites, and $\text{AgNO}_2$ gives nitroalkanes.

Answer: AgCN (alco)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is exhibited only by primary amines?
questions.solution:
Acetylation is given by both primary and secondary amines as they contain replaceable hydrogen atoms on the nitrogen atom.

Alkylation is given by primary, secondary, and tertiary amines to form higher amines and quaternary ammonium salts.

Reaction with nitrous acid is given by primary, secondary, and tertiary amines, though they yield different products (primary amines yield alcohols or diazonium salts, secondary amines yield N-nitrosamines, and tertiary amines yield nitrite salts).

The carbylamine test (isocyanide test) involves heating an amine with chloroform and alcoholic potassium hydroxide. Only primary aliphatic and aromatic amines give this test, producing foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamines). Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reagents is used to convert -CN group to -$\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ group?
questions.solution:
The conversion of a cyano group ($-CN$) to a primary amine group ($-CH_2NH_2$) is a reduction reaction.

Sodium and ethanol ($Na + C_2H_5OH$) act as a reducing agent, providing nascent hydrogen which reduces the nitrile to a primary amine. This reaction is known as the Mendius reduction.

$R-CN + 4[H] \xrightarrow{Na + C_2H_5OH} R-CH_2NH_2$

The other reagents are not reducing agents for this conversion: $CrO_3$ is an oxidizing agent, while $H_3PO_4$ and $Al_2O_3$ are typically used for dehydration.

Answer: $\text{Na} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when RCN is treated with sodium and alcohol.
questions.solution:
The reduction of alkyl cyanides (nitriles) with sodium and alcohol is known as the Mendius reduction.

In this reaction, the cyano group ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$) is reduced to a primary amine group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{R-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2$

The product obtained is a primary amine, $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following amines exhibits carbylamine test?
questions.solution:
The carbylamine test is a characteristic test for primary amines.

When a primary amine is heated with chloroform and alcoholic potassium hydroxide, it forms an isocyanide (carbylamine) which has a characteristic foul smell.

The reaction is given by:

$R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow R-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$

Secondary and tertiary amines do not give this test.

Answer: Primary amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when nitro ethane is treated with $\mathrm{Sn}-\mathrm{HCl}$ under ideal conditions.
questions.solution:
Tin with hydrochloric acid reduces nitro compounds to primary amines through the general reaction:

$\mathrm{R-NO_2 \xrightarrow{Sn/HCl} R-NH_2}$

For nitroethane, the ethyl group remains intact, yielding ethanamine.

A) Ethanamine ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$) corresponds to this product.

B) Acetamide and C) Formamide are amides, not amines, and do not result from nitro reduction.

D) Methanamine lacks the carbon skeleton of the starting material.

The product is ethanamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of allylamine?
questions.solution:
Allylamine has the structure $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-NH_2}$. The longest carbon chain containing both the double bond and amino group is three carbons. Numbering prioritizes the amino group as the principal functional group, giving it position 1. This places the double bond between carbons 2 and 3, so the parent chain is prop-2-ene. With the amino group at C1, the complete IUPAC name is prop-2-en-1-amine.

Evaluating the options:
A) Propan-1-amine corresponds to $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2}$ (saturated)
B) Prop-2-en-1-amine matches $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-NH_2}$
C) Prop-1-en-2-amine would be $\mathrm{CH_2=C(NH_2)-CH_3}$
D) Propan-2-amine is $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)CH_3}$ (saturated)

The correct IUPAC name is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is Hofmann exhaustive alkylation?
questions.solution:
Hofmann exhaustive alkylation describes the reaction of an amine with excess alkyl halide to form a quaternary ammonium salt through successive alkylation steps.

Option A shows Hofmann bromamide degradation, converting an amide to a primary amine with one less carbon. Option C depicts Hofmann elimination, decomposing a quaternary ammonium salt to form an alkene and tertiary amine. Option D represents nitrile reduction to a primary amine (Mendius reduction).

Option B corresponds exactly to Hofmann exhaustive alkylation: $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{excess}]{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{X}} \mathrm{R}_4 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{N}} \overline{\mathrm{X}}$.

The reaction proceeds through successive nucleophilic substitutions where the primary amine is progressively alkylated to secondary, tertiary, and finally quaternary ammonium salt.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify tertiary amine from following.
questions.solution:
Tertiary amines are characterized by a nitrogen atom bonded to three alkyl or aryl groups, with no hydrogen substituents.

Cyclohexanamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NH}_2$) contains nitrogen bonded to one cyclohexyl group and two hydrogen atoms, making it a primary amine.

Ethane 1,2-diamine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}_2$) contains two nitrogen atoms, each bonded to an alkyl fragment and two hydrogens, classifying it as a primary diamine.

N-Phenylbenzeneamine ($(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$) contains nitrogen bonded to two phenyl groups and one hydrogen, designating it as a secondary amine.

N-Ethyl-N-Methylpropan-2-amine ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{N}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)(\text{CH}_3)$) contains nitrogen bonded to an isopropyl group, an ethyl group, and a methyl group. With three alkyl substituents and no hydrogen atoms, this is a tertiary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify least stable species from following.
questions.solution:
Electron-donating groups stabilize positively charged species through the +I effect, with alkyl groups providing increasing stabilization as their number increases.

$\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ lacks alkyl substituents and receives no inductive stabilization from electron-donating groups.

$\mathrm{R-NH_3+}$ gains modest stabilization from one alkyl group, while $\mathrm{R_2NH_2^+}$ benefits more strongly from two alkyl groups. $\mathrm{R_3NH^+}$ achieves maximum stability through three electron-donating alkyl groups.

The stability order follows the number of alkyl substituents: $\mathrm{R_3NH^+ \gt R_2NH_2+ \gt RNH_3+ \gt NH_4^+}$.

The least stable species is therefore $\mathrm{NH4^+}$, corresponding to option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the expected order of basic strength of different compounds from following.
questions.solution:
The basic strength of amines is determined by the availability of nitrogen's lone pair for donation. Alkyl groups exert an inductive effect, increasing electron density on nitrogen. Based solely on this effect, basicity increases with alkyl substitution: $\mathrm{NH}_3 \lt \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}_2 \lt \mathrm{R}_2 \mathrm{NH} \lt \mathrm{R}_3 \mathrm{N}$.

In aqueous solution, solvation effects and steric hindrance become significant. The conjugate acid's stability through hydrogen bonding decreases with increased alkyl substitution: $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$ forms 4 H-bonds, $\mathrm{RNH}_3^+$ forms 3, $\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{NH}_2^+$ forms 2, and $\mathrm{R}_3\mathrm{NH}^+$ forms 1. This reverses the order expected from induction alone.

In the gas phase, solvation is absent and the inductive effect dominates, yielding the order $\mathrm{NH}_3 \lt \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}_2 \lt \mathrm{R}_2 \mathrm{NH} \lt \mathrm{R}_3 \mathrm{N}$. Option B matches this order precisely.

questions.q: Which from following compounds is an example of primary amines?
questions.solution:
A primary amine has the nitrogen atom bonded to one alkyl or aryl group and two hydrogen atoms.

N-methylmethanamine: Contains a methyl group substitution on nitrogen, resulting in the structure $\mathrm{CH_3-NH-CH_3}$, making it secondary.

4-Bromobenzenamine: Consists of a single aryl group and two hydrogens on nitrogen, conforming to $\mathrm{Ar-NH_2}$, hence primary.

N-Phenylbenzenamine: Nitrogen bonds to two aryl groups as $\mathrm{C_6 H_5-NH-C_6 H_5}$, classifying it as secondary.

N-Ethyl-N-methylpropan-2-amine: The structure is $\mathrm{(CH_3)2CH-N(CH_3)(C_2H_5)}$ with three alkyl groups attached, rendering it tertiary.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of H atoms required for complete reduction of one mole acetonitrile?
questions.solution:
Reduction of acetonitrile follows the general catalytic hydrogenation reaction for nitriles: $R-C\equiv N + 2H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{catalyst}} R-CH_2NH_2$.

For acetonitrile ($CH_3CN$): $CH_3-C\equiv N + 2H_2 \rightarrow CH_3CH_2NH_2$.

Each mole of $H_2$ contains 2 moles of hydrogen atoms, so 2 moles of $H_2$ yield $2 \times 2 = 4$ moles of H atoms.

The complete reduction of one mole of acetonitrile requires 4 moles of H atoms.

Option D, $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{NH}_2$, is a primary amine, undergoes the reaction, and produces the foul-smelling ethyl isocyanide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the medium required for formation of p-Hydroxyazobenzene from benzene diazonium chloride and phenol.
questions.solution:
The electrophilic aromatic substitution between benzene diazonium chloride and phenol requires specific pH conditions.

The diazonium cation $C_6H_5N_2^+$ acts as an electrophile, while phenol must be in its deprotonated phenoxide form $C_6H_5O^-$ to serve as an effective nucleophile.

A mild alkaline medium (typically pH $9$–$10$) facilitates this deprotonation, enhancing nucleophilicity and enabling efficient coupling at the para position.

Acidic conditions protonate the diazonium group or suppress phenol dissociation, while neutral or non-aqueous solvents lack the necessary basicity.

The correct condition is therefore a mild alkaline medium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines has lowest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$ value?
questions.solution:
Identifying the amine with the lowest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$ reveals the strongest base among the given options.

Ethylamine ($\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{2}$) is a primary aliphatic amine where the ethyl group donates electrons via the +I effect, enhancing nitrogen's electron density and basicity; $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}} \approx 3.25$.

Trimethylamine ($(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{3}\mathrm{N}$) is a tertiary aliphatic amine with significant +I effects, but steric hindrance reduces solvation of its conjugate acid, lowering basicity; $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}} \approx 4.20$.

Aniline ($\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{2}$) is an aromatic amine with resonance delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the benzene ring, drastically reducing basicity; $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}} \approx 9.38$.

Benzylamine ($\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{NH}_{2}$) is a primary amine where the phenyl group exerts a weak -I effect through the methylene spacer, with no resonance delocalization; it is less basic than ethylamine but stronger than aniline; $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}} \approx 4.67$.

Comparing $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$ values, ethylamine has the lowest at approximately $3.25$, confirming it as the strongest base.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify correct decreasing order of basic strength of amines from following.
questions.solution:
Amine basicity in aqueous solution is governed by three competing factors: inductive effects, solvation, and steric hindrance.

Alkyl groups donate electrons through the +I effect, increasing electron density on nitrogen and enhancing basicity. This would suggest the order: tertiary > secondary > primary amine.

However, aqueous solvation stabilizes the conjugate acid through hydrogen bonding. Primary amines form three H-bonds ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3^+$), secondary amines two ($(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}_2^+$), and tertiary amines only one ($(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{NH}^+$). Solvation alone would produce the order: primary > secondary > tertiary.

Tertiary amines additionally experience steric hindrance from bulky groups, further reducing basicity.

The observed order results from balancing these effects: secondary amines optimize inductive gain and solvation, while tertiary amines suffer from poor solvation and steric effects. The experimental order is:

$(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH} \gt \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 \gt (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N}$

Option B matches this sequence.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.solution:
The basic strength of amines in aqueous solution depends on three competing factors: inductive effects, solvation effects, and steric hindrance.

Alkyl groups exert an electron-donating inductive effect (+I), increasing electron density on the nitrogen atom and enhancing basicity. Solvation stabilizes the conjugate acid through hydrogen bonding: $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$ forms 4 H-bonds, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3^+$ forms 3, $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}_2^+$ forms 2, and $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{NH}^+$ forms only 1. $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}$ achieves optimal balance with strong inductive effects and adequate solvation, making it the strongest base. $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2$ follows with moderate inductive and solvation effects. $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N}$ has maximal inductive effect but suffers from poor solvation and steric hindrance. $\mathrm{NH}_3$, lacking inductive donation, is weakest despite excellent solvation.

The experimentally observed order is $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH} \gt \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 \gt (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N} \gt \mathrm{NH}_3$, corresponding to increasing order $\mathrm{NH}_3 \lt (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N} \lt \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 \lt (\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}$.

Dimethylamine $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2 \mathrm{NH}$ benefits from inductive effects and favorable solvation, making it the strongest base.

Aniline is the weakest base due to resonance stabilization, giving it the highest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.solution:
Base strength in aqueous solution depends on the balance between inductive effects, steric hindrance, and solvation stability.

Alkyl groups donate electron density through the $+I$ effect, increasing nitrogen's basicity. However, larger alkyl groups introduce steric hindrance and reduce conjugate acid solvation through hydrogen bonding.

For methyl-substituted amines: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}$ provides optimal balance with strong inductive effect from two methyl groups, moderate steric hindrance, and adequate solvation of its conjugate acid $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}_2^+$ which forms two hydrogen bonds.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2$ has weaker inductive effect and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ has no alkyl groups, while $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N}$ suffers from significant steric hindrance and poor solvation of its conjugate acid.

The basicity order is secondary > primary > tertiary > ammonia, making $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH}$ the strongest base.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following reaction results in azo coupling?
questions.solution:
Azo coupling is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction involving an arenediazonium salt and an electron-rich aromatic compound like phenol or aniline, forming an azo compound with the $\mathrm{-N=N-}$ linkage, often used as dyes.

A: Aniline reacts with nitrous acid to form benzenediazonium chloride ($\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$). This is diazotization, producing a precursor, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + HNO_2 + HCl \xrightarrow{0-5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}} C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + 2H_2O}$.

B: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with phenol in alkaline medium, coupling at the para-position due to the activating hydroxyl group: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + C_6H_5OH \xrightarrow{OH^-} C_6H_5-N=N-C_6H_4-OH\ (p) + HCl}$. This is a classic azo coupling.

C: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with $\mathrm{HBF_4}$ to form diazonium fluoroborate, an intermediate in the Balz-Schieman reaction for fluorobenzene synthesis, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + HBF_4 \rightarrow C_6H_5N_2^+BF_4^- + HCl}$.

D: Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes substitution with copper powder and HCl to form chlorobenzene, known as the Gattermann reaction, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- \xrightarrow[\mathrm{HCl}]{Cu\ (Powder)} C_6H_5Cl + N_2}$.

Thus, only option B represents an azo coupling reaction.
